messages:
Tess (PM): Quick sync: customer feedback says org-level spend is confusing when invoices are only per-project. Need proposal for UI that clarifies scope + export options. @Arun take a pass? Arun (Design): Two ideas: 1) persistent scope chip (Org / Project) near top-left of the usage page, with a subtle badge that shows \"invoices: project-only\" when relevant; 2) add an export dropdown on the header with options: CSV (visible rows), Invoice (if available), Consolidated export (experimental). Lina (Frontend): Persistent chip is doable. Concern: header real estate on small screens. We can collapse text into icon + tooltip at <640px. Export dropdown is fine but fetching invoice links for each row will need lazy calls. Jordan (Accessibility): Scope chip MUST have an accessible label that includes current scope and invoice scope, e.g., aria-label=\"Viewing: Organization (invoices available per project)\". Also ensure dropdown keyboard nav cycles and that the export actions are announced. Kai (Backend): We already expose invoice metadata per-project via billing service. For consolidated export, we can generate a server-side CSV job (async). Might be a day or two of work + small quota for heavy accounts. Tess (PM): Important: reduce mistakes where customers think invoice = visible CSV. Copy needs to be explicit. Draft microcopy: \"Invoices are issued per project. Use Export > Consolidate to generate a combined CSV for accounting.\" Thoughts? Arun (Design): Microcopy tweak: make the call-to-action link to a tooltip/modal \"How invoices work\" rather than inline text. Keeps the row tidy. Also propose an inline tiny badge that shows \"project invoices only\" in orange for attention (but Jordan, will that pass contrast?) Jordan (Accessibility): Orange badge is ok if contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 against background. Prefer using an outline badge rather than filled for better contrast with white backgrounds. Also ensure tooltip triggered by focus and hover, not just hover. Lina (Frontend): Implementation note: badge as might be noisy for screen readers. Better to include the invoice note in aria-describedby for the table and keep the visible badge decorative (aria-hidden=true). UXBot: Lint: table header cell \"Spend (30d)\" ambiguous. Recommend \"Spend (last 30 days, est.)\" or make rounding explicit. Tess (PM): Good catch. Let's use \"Spend (last 30 days, estimated)\" — that should reduce support tickets. Arun (Design): Also thinking about sorting: default sort should be by cost desc for org view, but project view should default to tokens desc. Will show wireframes. Kai (Backend): Sorting switches are cheap in the API. We should remember to include stable sort key to avoid flicker when paginating. Lina (Frontend): For the export dropdown markup, suggestion below. We'll lazy-load invoice links only when the dropdown opens to avoid N+1 calls: ```html
  • CSV (visible rows)
  • Invoice (project) — lazy load
  • Consolidated export (async)
``` Jordan (Accessibility): Good. Also ensure menu keyboard handling: arrow keys to move, esc to close, open triggers focus on first item. Add aria-busy when lazy-loading invoice links. Tess (PM): Decision for next sprint: 1) Add persistent scope chip with tooltip/modal explaining invoice scope, responsive icon for mobile. 2) Add Export dropdown, lazy-load invoice links when menu opens, and surface consolidated export as an async job. 3) Update spend header copy to \"Spend (last 30 days, estimated)\". 4) Default sorting: org=cost desc, project=tokens desc. Arun (Design): I'll post updated mockups in figma with mobile variants and show the orange-outline badge option vs plain chip. Lina (Frontend): I'll prototype the header and export menu, including lazy fetch behavior and small telemetry event for consolidated export. Jordan (Accessibility): I'll prepare a short QA checklist (keyboard nav, aria labels, contrast checks, live-region announcements for async export). Tess (PM): Thanks team! We'll review estimates tomorrow. :raised_hands:
